title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Mo asked your assistant about laser-cutter training on Monday. That conversation was never saved anywhere. On Thursday, Mo opens a brand-new session and asks, "Can I use the laser cutter now?" What does the model see when it is first called for this question?

options.text: Mo's entire Monday conversation, because the model remembers every student it has talked to
Only this session's system prompt, tool definitions, and Mo's new question, with nothing from Monday
A short summary of Monday's chat that the model wrote for itself automatically before it ended
Nothing at first, but Monday's details return as soon as Mo mentions the laser cutter by name

items.stem: Within one session, your assistant's model calls check_training_record, then search_manuals, then writes its final answer. Compared with its very first call that session, what is different about its input on the call where it writes the final answer?

options.text: It is shorter, because older tool results are dropped automatically once newer ones arrive
It is longer: it now includes the first call's content plus both tool results, kept in full
It is the same length, because the newest tool result simply replaces the original question
It is longer only if the program is specifically told to make the model remember earlier steps

items.stem: Your sponsor suggests switching to a model with a much bigger context window, so the assistant can "just remember everything" between visits without saving anything to a database. What is the problem with this plan?

options.text: A bigger window still starts empty at the beginning of a new session; it carries nothing over from a past one
A bigger window would work for this, it would simply cost more on every single call than a smaller one
A bigger window makes the model slower at reading whatever question is asked this session
A bigger window only holds images and manuals, and cannot hold any conversation history at all

items.stem: Your assistant answers questions from a 40-page machine manual using a search_manuals tool. In one or two sentences, why is retrieving just the relevant page with a tool call better than loading the whole manual into context on every question?
Your team is deciding where to keep the fact that a student completed laser-cutter training, so the assistant can check it weeks later. Which is the right place for that fact to live?

options.text: In the model's context window, repeated at the top of every student's prompt from now on
In a persistent record outside the model, such as a database row the check_training_record tool reads
Nowhere in particular; the model will infer it from how the student phrases later questions
In the model's training data, by fine-tuning it on this one student's record
